page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number 299 at top right. Main text in one full-width block of verse, then a woodcut ornament, a centred title with subtitle, then a prose paragraph. Marginal notes in the right margin beside the verse and the prose.

main_text.l: Porticibus, sacros iuuenum certamine lucos?
Quid tot captiuis fulgentia culmina rostris?
Armáque fixa deis? aut qua Marathonius hostis
Perdidit, aut Libya quae sunt aduecta subacta?
Hic Agathocleis sedes ornata trophais,Agathocles Rex Siciliae. Hieron.
Hic mitis Hieronis opes, hic sancta vetustas
Artificum manibus, non vsquam clarior vllo
Gloria pictura seclo: non aera vocabant
Quae scirent Ephyren: suluo certaret vt auro
Vestis spirantes referens sub tegmine vultus,
Qua radio celat Babylon, vel murice picto
Lata Tyros, quae Attalicis variata per artem
Aulaeis scribuntur acu, aut Memphitide tela.Ausonius de clar. vrbibus.
Quis Catinam sileat? quis quadruplices Syracusas?
Hinc ambustorum fratrum pietate celebrem,Catina Catinaxi fratres.
Illam complexam miracula fontis & amnis.
Quam maris Ionij subter vada falsa meantes
Confociant dulces placita sibi sede liquores,
Incorruptarum miscentes oscula aquarum.
Vtq; Syracusas Arethusidas abstulit armisFast. lib. 4.
Claudius, & bello te quoque cepit, Eryx.
main_text.head: MARE IONIVM, CVIVS & Adriaticum pars est.
main_text.p: Deinceps autem maris ad Ionij ortumDionysius. Absyrti insularum apparet immensus tractus, Absyrti insulae.Quas olim Colchorum filij incurrarunt, quando defessi fuerunt. Vestigia indagantes vagabunda Aetea.
Deinceps autem post has Liburnica sita sunt.

page.notes: The woodcut ornament above the title is not transcribed. Lines of verse on the page are the printed Latin; the first paragraph of prose begins with a large initial D. Some marginal notes are only partly legible and were transcribed as best read. Note "Fast. lib. 4." and "Catina Catinaxi fratres" are uncertain at the marked places.
